requirements.title: Image selectors determine image indices for coindexed objects
requirements.definition: An image selector is the syntactic selector that determines the image index for a coindexed object. The bracket form, cosubscript scalar integer syntax, optional selector-spec list, team selection, cobound validity, and STAT/NOTIFY effects are specified by the more specific 9.6 requirements and by the data-ref/part-ref owners that admit image selectors on coarrays.

The oracle distinguishes the local image index from image 1 without using addresses, TRANSFER, undefined storage, or compiler agreement.

The controls observe literal values 31 and 41 respectively; a malformed bracket/parenthesis swap is attributable to the relevant R926 image-selector or array-subscript owner, not to coarray declaration rules.

requirements.title: An image selector is a bracketed cosubscript list with an optional selector-spec list
requirements.definition: The grammar for image-selector is exactly lbracket cosubscript-list optionally followed by a comma and an image-selector-spec-list, then rbracket. The cosubscript-list is required and precedes any selector specs. Parentheses are array/substring syntax, not R926 image-selector delimiters.

requirements.title: An image selector spec is NOTIFY, STAT, TEAM, or TEAM_NUMBER
requirements.definition: The grammar for image-selector-spec admits exactly one of four keyword forms: NOTIFY=notify-variable, STAT=stat-variable, TEAM=team-value, or TEAM_NUMBER=scalar-int-expr. R928 admits the forms; C932 prohibits repeated specifiers, C934 prohibits TEAM and TEAM_NUMBER in the same selector-spec list, C933 restricts NOTIFY placement, and p3/p6/p7 specify the team and STAT effects.

The later NOTIFY WAIT observation of a single count, under a multi-image gated profile, is the independent oracle; type and noncoindexed notify-variable requirements stay dependencies.

pending.team-number-selector-spec: PENDING positive-control source: in the initial team, use x[1, TEAM_NUMBER=TEAM_NUMBER()] with x established in the initial team. requirements.definition: Within a given image-selector-spec-list, no specifier keyword shall appear more than once. Distinct specifiers may appear together subject to the independent C933 NOTIFY placement rule, C934 TEAM/TEAM_NUMBER mutual exclusion, C935 STAT variable rule, and the prose team/STAT requirements.

requirements.title: Cosubscript values are within cobounds and determine image index by coarray subscript order
requirements.definition: For an image selector, each cosubscript value shall be within the cobounds for its codimension. Taking account of those cobounds, the cosubscript list determines the image index in the same way that an array-element subscript list determines a subscript order value in 9.5.3.3. The separate statement that the number of cosubscripts equals the object's corank is recorded here as dependent on the registered C914 owner.

requirements.title: TEAM selects the current or an ancestor team and requires establishment in that team
requirements.definition: If a TEAM= specifier appears in an image selector, the team of the image selector is specified by team-value. That team-value shall identify the current team or an ancestor team, and the selected object shall be an established coarray in that team. The TEAM_TYPE value and CHANGE TEAM/FORM TEAM mechanisms that create valid team values are dependencies.

requirements.title: An image selector specifies an existing image index in its selected team
requirements.definition: An image selector shall specify an image index value that is not greater than the number of images in the team of the image selector. That image index identifies the image with that index in that team. The selected team is supplied by p3, and the image index value is determined from the cosubscript list under p2.

pending.image-index-within-team-size: PENDING positive-control source: under a declared one-image profile, x[1] selects image 1; under a declared at-least-two-image profile, x[2] selects image 2. The oracle is distinct per-image literals and NUM_IMAGES() establishing the profile before selection.
pending.image-index-identifies-image-in-team: PENDING multi-image positive-control source: in two different teams, use the same image index 1 with different per-team literals. The oracle distinguishes the image with index 1 in the selected team, not the same physical process or address.
pending.image-index-too-large-invalid: PENDING source/diagnostic-policy plan: under a profile proving NUM_IMAGES()==1 for the selected team, attempt x[2] with otherwise valid coarray syntax and establishment. Repair to x[1] and observe a literal. The invalidity is attributable to p5; the invalid source must not be executed by referencing a nonexistent image, and no mandatory static diagnostic is claimed for runtime-valued image counts.

requirements.title: STAT in an image selector defines the STAT variable with failed-image or zero status
requirements.definition: Execution of a statement containing an image-selector with a STAT= specifier causes the stat-variable to become defined. If the designator is part of an operand that is evaluated or is a variable being defined or partly defined, and the object designated is on a failed image, the stat-variable is defined with STAT_FAILED_IMAGE from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV; otherwise it is defined with zero.

pending.stat-variable-defined: PENDING positive-control source: initialize local scalar INTEGER s=-99, execute a statement containing x[1, STAT=s] on a nonfailed image, and observe that s is no longer -99. The selected x literal is also checked so the statement is reached.
pending.stat-zero-on-nonfailed-image: PENDING positive-control source: read or define x[1, STAT=s] where image 1 is nonfailed and x contains literal 171. The oracle is selected/assigned literal plus s=0, independent of any compiler message.
pending.stat-failed-image-value: PENDING multi-image failed-image profile source: after a separately qualified image failure that the processor can detect, execute a reference or definition of x[failed_index, STAT=s] and observe s==STAT_FAILED_IMAGE without using the referenced value as an oracle. This remains pending until failed-image detection is a gated suite capability.
pending.failed-image-premise-limited-to-evaluate: PENDING source plan with a statement containing an image selector in a context whose designator is not evaluated, contrasted with an evaluated operand or variable definition. The oracle is the resulting STAT value (zero versus STAT_FAILED_IMAGE under a detected failed-image setup), never the value of a coindexed object on a failed image.

requirements.title: STAT variables in image selectors are independent of same-statement evaluation and side effects
requirements.definition: The denotation of a stat-variable in an image selector shall not depend on the evaluation of any entity in the same statement. The value of an expression shall not depend on the value of any stat-variable that appears in the same statement. The value of a stat-variable in an image selector shall not be affected by execution of any part of the statement, except through whether the image specified by the image selector has failed.

pending.stat-variable-denotation-independent: PENDING source/diagnostic-policy pair: use STAT=s(k) where k is also evaluated in the same assignment statement, with s a local INTEGER array and all bounds valid; repair by using a separate scalar STAT variable s0. The repaired oracle is selected literal 181 and s0=0. The invalidity is attributable to p7 denotation dependence, not C935 or scalar-int-variable syntax.
pending.expression-value-independent-of-stat-var: PENDING source/diagnostic-policy pair: attempt y = x[1, STAT=s] + s with s previously defined and x[1] otherwise valid. Repair by using a saved copy s_before or by removing s from the expression, and observe a literal result plus s=0. The invalidity is attributable to p7 expression-value dependence.
pending.stat-variable-value-not-otherwise-affect: PENDING source/diagnostic-policy pair: attempt s = x[1, STAT=s] or another statement that also defines the same scalar STAT variable apart from the image failure condition. Repair by using a separate left-hand variable and observe selected literal 183 with s=0. The invalidity is attributable to p7 side-effect limitation, not to p6 STAT definition itself.
